headline: POCA Allows 2-Year Renewable Detention; Federal Court Voided Its Review Ban in 2022
context: The Prevention of Crime Act 1959, amended in 2014, lets an appointed Prevention Board impose 2-year detention orders with no cap on renewals. In April 2022 the Federal Court struck down section 15B, which had barred courts from reviewing Board decisions.

changes.summary: Correction: Removed an unverified count of 420 POCA detainees and an 87% lower-income figure. The issue now centres on renewable two-year orders, the 2014 removal of judicial review and Article 149.
Correction: Narrowed the judicial-review point: section 15B bars review of the Board's discretion, but courts keep jurisdiction on procedural grounds.

cards.big: POCA detention orders run 2 years and can be renewed without limit. The clause that shielded the Board from the courts has been void since April 2022.
cards.sub: The Federal Court struck down section 15B and section 4, on police remand, for breaching the separation of powers.

cards.big: In April 2022 a five-member Federal Court bench chaired by the Chief Justice struck down POCA sections 4 and 15B.
cards.sub: Section 7B: Board members are appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong. The Act provides for Inquiry Officer reports and Board decisions.

cards.big: Article 5 protects personal liberty. POCA operates as a special law under Article 149.
cards.sub: Article 149 validates such laws despite inconsistency with Articles 5, 9, 10 or 13.

cards.big: SUHAKAM and Suaram raised concern in January 2019 about children detained under POCA.
cards.sub: The Act, as reprinted in 2018, sets no duty to report detention outcomes to Parliament.

cards.big: POCA is not an Article 150 emergency ordinance. It is standing law, and since 2022 its Board answers to the courts.
Like a registered-person watchlist decided by an appointed committee, with detention as the operating consequence.
cards.sub: Preventive detention allows confinement without a criminal trial. Article 151 provides limited procedural safeguards via an advisory board.

cards.big: Judges, not legislators, reopened POCA detention to court review. Two-year renewable detention without trial remains the law.
